Neovim tips from my setup: flash, smart splits and sending code to a REPL

I write most of my code in Neovim. The configuration started from NvChad and grew with plugins managed by lazy.nvim. These are the habits from it that pay off every single day, in the order I would teach them.

flash.nvim: jump anywhere in two keystrokes

flash.nvim replaces a lot of counting and scrolling. Press s, type one or two characters of the place you want, and every match gets a label. Press the label and the cursor is there. My mappings:

{ "s", mode = { "n", "x", "o" }, function() require("flash").jump() end },
{ "S", mode = { "n", "x", "o" }, function() require("flash").treesitter() end },
{ "r", mode = "o", function() require("flash").remote() end },
{ "R", mode = { "o", "x" }, function() require("flash").treesitter_search() end },
  • s jumps to any visible text.
  • S selects syntax nodes (a call, an argument, a function) through treesitter.
  • r in operator-pending mode is the remote action: yank or delete something far away without moving the cursor.

Small remaps that add up

map("n", ";", ":")            -- command mode without Shift
map("i", "jj", "<ESC>")        -- leave insert mode on the home row
map("n", "H", "^")            -- start of the line
map("n", "L", "$")            -- end of the line
map("i", "<C-s>", "<ESC>:w<CR>")  -- save from anywhere

smart-splits: one set of keys for splits and panes

With smart-splits.nvim, Ctrl-h/j/k/l moves between splits and Alt-h/j/k/l resizes them. Because it is aware of the terminal multiplexer, the same keys move across tmux panes when I reach the edge of the editor, so I never think about where the editor ends and the terminal begins.

vim-slime: send code to a REPL

For analysis I want to run code line by line, like in a notebook, but without leaving the editor. vim-slime sends the current line or selection to a terminal buffer in Neovim. The terminal is chosen by file type:

python = "uv run python",
r      = "R",
sql    = "duckdb ",

So a Python file talks to a uv-managed Python, an R file to R and a SQL file to DuckDB.

Format, lint and test from the editor

  • conform.nvim and nvim-lint run ruff; one mapping formats the file and organises imports.
  • Another mapping toggles pyright diagnostics when the type checker is too noisy for exploration.
  • neotest with nvim-dap-python runs and debugs the test under the cursor.

Other tools one key away

yazi (file manager), lazygit and fzf-lua all open inside Neovim, quarto-nvim handles Quarto documents with the embedded code in the right language, and persistence.nvim restores the session when I come back to a project. The AI helpers (CodeCompanion and friends) live behind a <leader>a prefix so they never get in the way.

If you only take one thing from this list, take flash. It is the single plugin that changed how fast I move through code.
